IB Gram shares an actual fee range once the grade, current writing level and weekly frequency are known, rather than a flat number quoted upfront.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring good enough for a writing-heavy subject like English?
faqs.answer: Yes, more often than parents expect, particularly for feedback-based writing work. Shared documents let a tutor mark up a student's actual paragraph in real time, which works at least as well as sitting side by side, sometimes better since the marked version stays with the student to review afterward. Where online tutoring struggles more is with younger students who need in-person presence to stay focused during a reading session. For senior-stage exam technique specifically, online is often the stronger choice because it opens access to specialists who know this syllabus's mark scheme well.

faqs.question: We're near Chanakyapuri and travel internationally often — how does that affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: It's worth mentioning upfront, since families connected to embassy postings or frequent travel often need a schedule that flexes around trips rather than a rigid weekly slot. Online tutoring tends to suit this pattern better than home tutoring, since sessions can continue from wherever the family happens to be, and a tutor familiar with mid-year arrivals or gaps in continuity can adjust the plan accordingly. IB Gram asks about this kind of scheduling pattern directly rather than assuming every Delhi family follows a standard, unbroken term calendar.

faqs.question: What if my child's tutor keeps arriving late because of traffic?
faqs.answer: That's a legitimate reason to ask for a change, not something to just tolerate. A tutor who is frequently late because their base is genuinely far from your area, or whose route through South Delhi traffic is unreliable at the requested time, isn't a sustainable long-term match regardless of how good they are as a teacher. IB Gram would rather know about this pattern early and either adjust the schedule, switch to an online arrangement, or find a tutor whose regular route actually fits, than let it quietly continue term after term.

faqs.question: How does IB Gram handle switching tutors if the fit isn't right?
faqs.answer: Straightforwardly, and without treating it as an inconvenience. If a tutor's pace, feedback style or personality isn't working for the student after a few sessions, that gets flagged and a different tutor gets suggested based on what specifically didn't work. Sometimes it's about explanation style, sometimes about the schedule not actually holding up in practice. Raising it after two or three sessions, rather than persevering for a full term, tends to get a family to the right match faster.

faqs.question: My child reads well but writes weak paragraphs — is that an English tutor's job or something else?
faqs.answer: It's squarely an English tutor's job, and it's a common and specific gap — reading comprehension and writing production are related but different skills, and being strong at one doesn't guarantee the other. A tutor should be able to isolate whether the issue is planning, not organising ideas before writing, execution, weak topic sentences or unclear evidence use, or simply unfamiliarity with what this syllabus's directed writing tasks actually reward. Naming that gap precisely, rather than assuming general writing practice will fix it, usually produces faster improvement.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with the American Embassy School, DPS International Saket, The British School New Delhi, the IB Organization, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. faqs.question: What if we're starting tutoring close to the November exam session?
faqs.answer: It's still worth starting, but the plan narrows. A few weeks before an exam session, the priority shifts from general writing development to exam-specific technique: comprehension question strategy, directed writing structure under a time limit, and reviewing past papers against the actual mark scheme. IB Gram is upfront that a compressed timeline means prioritising highest-impact skills over full, gradual writing development, and will say so plainly rather than promising broad improvement that a few weeks genuinely can't deliver.

faqs.question: Can one tutor manage both English and Economics for essay-writing support?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the tutor genuinely has strength in both — the two subjects share some argument-structuring skills, so a tutor comfortable with both can occasionally address a shared weak point in written expression more efficiently. But IB Gram doesn't default to this combination automatically; a tutor who is excellent at English but only adequate at Economics essay technique isn't necessarily the better choice over two separate specialists. Families are usually asked which subject is the more urgent concern before combining tutors for convenience.

faqs.question: How does scheduling work for families commuting from Gurugram or Noida?
faqs.answer: It's treated as a real factor, not an afterthought. A family commuting from Gurugram or Noida into a Delhi school often has less flexible evening time than one already based centrally, and that usually points toward online tutoring rather than adding a home tutor's own travel time on top of an already long day. IB Gram asks about the family's actual commute pattern when setting up a match, rather than assuming every Delhi-area family has the same amount of free evening time to work with.

introSummary: Parents typically search for an IGCSE Geography tutor in Delhi expecting a general subject expert who will simply cover the syllabus again, slower. What actually moves a grade is more specific: most students are losing marks on named case-study detail, map and graph interpretation, or structuring a longer written answer around command terms like assess or evaluate. IB Gram reviews the student's actual mock or school feedback before suggesting a tutor, then matches for home tutoring in South Delhi, online sessions, or a hybrid plan depending on what the gap really is.

contentBlocks.heading: What Parents Search For Versus What Actually Fixes the Grade
contentBlocks.body: The typical search goes something like this: a mock comes back weaker than expected, and the parent looks for the best IGCSE Geography tutor in Delhi, assuming the whole subject needs redoing. In practice, when the actual mock script or teacher feedback is reviewed, the pattern is usually narrower. A student might understand plate tectonics conceptually but cannot recall the specific named case study well enough to score full marks on a structured question that asks for it. Another might understand every topic but consistently loses marks on map reading, cross-sections or interpreting a data table under time pressure. A third writes accurate content but never actually answers the command term, describing a process when the question asked for an evaluation. These are three completely different fixes, and a generic full-syllabus re-teach solves none of them efficiently. This is why IB Gram asks for the actual mock paper or recent feedback before suggesting a tutor rather than matching purely on subject name. A parent in Delhi juggling school runs, traffic and a student's own extracurricular schedule does not have unlimited tutoring hours to spend on a diagnosis a first session should have caught. Getting the actual gap right before the first session saves weeks.

Map, cross-section and data-response interpretation
Answering the command term, not just the content
A generic full re-teach rarely fixes any of these efficiently
Actual mock feedback reviewed before a tutor is suggested

contentBlocks.heading: South and Central Delhi, and Where Online Takes Over

Even within this fairly compact stretch, Delhi traffic at peak evening hours can turn a short-distance booking into a genuine scheduling problem, and it is worth being upfront about that rather than promising a reliable weekly slot that later gets cancelled twice a month. Online tutoring is available across the whole city and does not carry this constraint, which is why it is often the better choice for a specific subject specialist rather than whoever happens to be reachable that evening. Families in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad who send their children to school in Delhi, or who are considering a Delhi-based tutor for schedule alignment with the school's own calendar, are also common requests, and online tutoring is usually the practical answer across that NCR spread rather than trying to coordinate travel across city lines for a weekly session. The honest guidance here is simple: home tutoring within a genuinely short travel radius works well; beyond that, online is not a fallback, it is the better option.

contentBlocks.heading: Matching the Format to the Actual Gap, Not the Other Way Around
contentBlocks.body: The three fixes named earlier each suit a different format. Case-study recall benefits from short, frequent online sessions where a tutor can quiz a student on named examples between school days, without needing to be physically present for what is essentially structured revision. Map and data-response skills often benefit from a shared screen where a tutor can annotate an actual past paper diagram live, which works cleanly online and does not require a physical whiteboard. Command-term and essay-structure problems benefit from a tutor reading a student's actual written answers closely and marking them against the criteria, again something that works well through shared documents regardless of location. Where home tutoring genuinely adds value in Delhi is with younger students who need someone present to build study habits and focus, or families who simply prefer an in-person routine for reasons beyond the subject itself. A hybrid plan — an occasional in-person session for structure and habit, online sessions for the actual subject work — suits many Delhi families given the travel realities described above. The point is to let the actual gap decide the format, rather than defaulting to home tutoring because it feels more serious, when for this subject it frequently is not the more effective choice.
items: Case-study recall: short, frequent online quizzing
Map and data skills: shared-screen annotation works well online
Essay structure: close marking via shared documents
Home tutoring: habit-building for younger students
Hybrid: in-person structure, online subject depth

Families commonly mention Math at AA or AI level, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A in the same conversation, since a Diploma-style student's week is genuinely full and Geography coursework or revision has to fit around deadlines in these other subjects, not exist in isolation. A Geography essay due the same week as an Economics internal assessment is a bad week to also start something new in a third subject, and IB Gram's review considers the full list a family mentions so that scheduling reflects the real pressure points in a student's calendar rather than treating each subject as its own island. Delhi students balancing school with extracurricular commitments — a common pattern here given how many families mention sports, music or debate schedules alongside academics — benefit particularly from this kind of whole-week view, since tutoring slots that ignore a fixed extracurricular commitment simply get missed or rescheduled repeatedly. For families where Geography genuinely is the only current concern, that is equally fine; the question is asked once so that advice fits the actual week a student is living, not an idealised one.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Suggested
contentBlocks.body: Before a tutor is suggested for IGCSE Geography, their actual teaching depth in the specific area a student needs is reviewed, distinguishing physical geography strength from human geography or skills-paper strength where relevant, rather than treating Geography as one undifferentiated subject. faqs.question: My child knows the topics but still loses marks in Geography. Why, and what fixes it?
faqs.answer: This is one of the most common patterns and it is usually a command-term problem rather than a knowledge gap: the student explains when the question asks them to evaluate, or describes when it asks for an assessment of impact. A tutor who checks this specifically, by reviewing actual past answers against the mark scheme, can usually correct it faster than a general content re-teach, often within a few focused sessions rather than a full term.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic in South Delhi given the traffic?
faqs.answer: It can be, for a genuinely short travel radius and a schedule that avoids the worst evening traffic windows, and IB Gram reviews requests across Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and nearby pockets on that basis. For families further apart or wanting a specific specialist regardless of location, online tutoring is usually more reliable week to week, since it removes the risk of a session being cancelled or shortened by a bad commute.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE Geography tuition cost in Delhi?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are home, online or hybrid, and how many sessions are needed weekly, so there is no single number quoted here. Sharing the grade, the actual gap if known, and the preferred mode gets a specific answer tied to a real available tutor, rather than a generic figure that may not match what is actually available at the time of the request.

faqs.question: Can online tutoring really help with map and diagram-based questions?
faqs.answer: Yes, often better than expected, since a tutor can share a screen and annotate an actual past paper map or graph live, which is close to how the student will interpret one in an actual exam anyway. What online cannot fully replace is a very young student's need for someone physically present to hold focus, but for the map-skills problem specifically, screen-based work is not a compromise.

faqs.question: We're based in Gurugram but our child studies in Delhi. Does that work?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is a common pattern, and online tutoring is usually the practical answer, since it lets a tutor align with the Delhi school's own calendar without needing to coordinate travel across NCR for a weekly slot. The same applies for families in Noida or Ghaziabad with children in Delhi schools; the school's timetable, not the family's home address, becomes the main scheduling factor.

faqs.question: How is progress actually tracked from week to week?
faqs.answer: A tutor is expected to share specific, visible updates rather than general reassurance: what was covered, what the student is still weak on, and what the plan is for the next session. For Geography specifically, useful markers include a case study the student can now recall fully, fewer marks lost on a timed map-skills exercise, or an essay that clearly answers the command term it was asked. Vague progress reports are worth questioning directly.

They are named on this page only because families frequently mention them when describing where they are based and how their school day is structured, not because of any partnership or endorsement arrangement with the schools themselves.

faqs.question: What if the tutor and my child don't get along after the first couple of sessions?
faqs.answer: This is not treated as a failed match to be pushed through out of politeness. A short conversation about what specifically was not working — pace, communication style, or something else entirely — helps identify a better fit quickly. The introductory step before paid sessions begin is meant to reduce how often this happens, though it does not eliminate it, and switching early is better than persisting for weeks hoping it improves on its own.

faqs.question: My child is only in Grade 8. Is it too early to start Geography-specific tutoring?
faqs.answer: IGCSE Geography as an exam subject typically starts a little later, so Grade 8 tutoring is usually better spent on general reading comprehension, structured writing and basic data-interpretation skills that will directly support Geography once it formally begins. Starting these foundations early tends to make the actual exam years noticeably less stressful, without needing subject-specific content before it is actually being taught in school.

faqs.question: What happens if there's no real improvement after a month of sessions?
faqs.answer: The first step is reviewing whether the original goal matched the actual gap identified at the start, since a mismatch between diagnosis and plan is a common cause of slow progress. If the tutor's approach is not working for the student specifically, IB Gram will look at a different match rather than insisting the family continue. If the goal itself was unrealistic for the timeline, that is discussed honestly, since Geography, like most humanities subjects, tends to improve in visible steps rather than smoothly.

introSummary: An IGCSE History tutor in Delhi is usually searched for at one of two moments: early in the term, when a new depth study or source-based topic has just started, or right before mocks, when gaps in source analysis and essay structure suddenly matter. Both moments call for different tutoring, and the honest answer to 'how late is too late' depends on which one you are in. Delhi families across South Delhi, central pockets and NCR commutes typically need this decided quickly, so IB Gram treats timing as the first question, not the last.

contentBlocks.heading: What's Due This Term Decides How Urgent This Search Is
contentBlocks.body: Before anything else, it helps to place your child on the calendar. A student in the early weeks of a new History unit has room to build source-analysis skills gradually — reading a document, weighing its origin and purpose, before writing a full essay under time pressure. A student three weeks from a school mock does not have that room, and the tutoring conversation changes completely: less concept-building, more targeted past-paper practice on the exact question types the mock will use. So how late is too late? Realistically, four to six weeks before an exam is still enough time to close specific gaps — weak essay structure, shaky source evaluation, thin factual recall on one or two topics — provided the student is willing to do focused practice between sessions, not just attend them. Starting in the final week rarely achieves more than familiarising a student with question formats; it will not rebuild a term's worth of missed content, and any tutor who claims otherwise is overselling. Delhi's academic calendar adds its own pressure, with many schools running assessments close together and students juggling extracurriculars on top. The honest first step is not choosing a tutor at all — it is being clear-eyed about how many real weeks remain and what is realistically fixable in that window.

contentBlocks.heading: Why Many Delhi Families End Up Choosing a Hybrid Plan
contentBlocks.body: Delhi's geography makes a single, fixed answer about tutoring mode unrealistic for a lot of families. A tutor based in South Delhi may manage weekly visits to Greater Kailash or Saket comfortably, and struggle to reach a student in a different part of the city on a weekday evening once traffic is accounted for. This is why many Delhi families end up choosing hybrid support rather than committing fully to one mode: home tutoring where travel is genuinely realistic, and online tutoring when a specific subject specialist matters more than physical proximity. For History specifically, online tutoring works well because most of the material — documents, extracts, past-paper questions — can be shared and annotated on screen just as clearly as on paper, and a student walking through an essay plan over video loses very little compared to doing it in person. Home tutoring still has real value for a student who focuses better with someone physically present, or a younger student building study habits from scratch. The trade-off worth naming honestly: hybrid only works smoothly if the family and tutor agree in advance on which weeks are in-person and which are online, rather than deciding informally each time, which tends to create the exact scheduling confusion hybrid was meant to avoid.

History transfers well to screen since most material is document- and text-based

contentBlocks.heading: History Rarely Travels Alone in a Delhi Household
contentBlocks.body: Most Delhi families requesting an IGCSE History tutor are also managing at least one other subject, and IB Gram's network in the city covers Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A alongside History. This matters for two practical reasons. First, a family can request support across subjects through one platform rather than running separate searches for each, and add a second subject later without repeating the entire background-check process. Second, a student combining History with English A benefits from a tutor aware that essay-writing skills genuinely transfer between the two — structuring an argument, using evidence precisely, writing under time pressure — even though the content is unrelated. This overlap does not mean the same tutor should teach both subjects. History rewards specific factual recall and source-evaluation skill that a general English tutor may not have, and an English A tutor's strength in literary analysis does not automatically make them good at historical argument. What is useful is a tutor, or a small coordinated pair of tutors, aware of how a student's writing habits in one subject are showing up in the other, since correcting an essay-structure problem once tends to help across both.

This is one of the clearest cases where online tutoring genuinely outperforms home tutoring rather than merely substituting for it. A History session built around reading a document and planning an essay works identically whether the tutor is five minutes away or across the city, and removing the commute means a slot that would otherwise be lost to traffic can go to actual teaching instead. contentBlocks.heading: What Four Weeks of Tutoring Should Actually Show
contentBlocks.body: By the end of a month, a parent should be able to see something specific: an essay the student wrote that scores better on structure than the one before it, a source-based question the student can now answer without hand-holding, or at least a clear weekly goal both student and tutor agreed on and can point back to. 'History is going well' is not a useful update on its own; ask what topic was covered and what the student can now do that they could not do four weeks earlier. IB Gram supports parent-visible weekly goals so this kind of check is possible without an uncomfortable conversation. This does not mean linear progress every single week — History essay-writing improves unevenly, and a student can sharpen source analysis while still struggling with timed writing under exam conditions, which is a normal stage, not a failure. If a month passes with no specific account of what has changed, that is a fair reason to ask questions or request a different tutor, and doing so is not an overreaction. Equally, a student starting six weeks before a mock with almost no essay practice behind them should not expect to be exam-ready by week four; a tutor being honest about that limitation is a better sign than one promising a full turnaround.

Parent-visible weekly goals replace guesswork about what is actually being covered

Availability, including comfort with the family's preferred mode and realistic weekly slots given Delhi's traffic patterns, is reviewed on a case-by-case basis rather than promised as fixed months in advance.

faqs.question: How late can I start IGCSE History tutoring before the exam and still see improvement?
faqs.answer: It depends on what exactly is missing. If the gap is essay structure or source-evaluation technique rather than content knowledge, four to six weeks of focused, consistent sessions can make a real difference. If entire topics were missed across the term, that same window is enough to prioritise the highest-value content rather than cover everything, but it will not replace a full term's teaching. Starting in the final week or two mainly helps with exam technique and calming nerves, not rebuilding missing knowledge, so it is worth being realistic about which situation you are actually in.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic if I live in Greater Kailash but the tutor is based elsewhere in Delhi?
faqs.answer: It depends on where 'elsewhere' actually is and what time of day the session falls at. A tutor already working with families near Saket or South Delhi generally may manage a Greater Kailash visit without much trouble, while a tutor based across the city could find weekday evening travel genuinely difficult once traffic is factored in. Rather than assuming distance on a map settles this, it is worth flagging your exact area when requesting a match so IB Gram can check real travel feasibility, or suggest online tutoring if a home visit is not practical.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE History tutor actually do in a first session?
faqs.answer: A first session is usually diagnostic. The tutor reviews what has been covered in school so far, looks at a recent essay or homework piece to see how the student structures an argument and handles evidence, and identifies whether the main gap is factual recall, source analysis, or exam technique under time pressure. This gives both the tutor and the family a realistic starting point, rather than assuming every student needs the same kind of help from week one.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE History tutoring cost in Delhi?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by the tutor's experience, the mode chosen and how many sessions a week the student needs, so IB Gram does not publish a single rate. A tutor visiting a South Delhi home twice weekly is priced differently from one running two online sessions a week, and closer-to-exam intensive revision blocks are usually costed separately from regular term-time tutoring. The clearest approach is sharing your requirements first — grade, calendar stage, area and preferred mode — and reviewing a quote against the specific tutor proposed.

faqs.question: Do you guarantee a grade improvement in History?
faqs.answer: No, and any platform claiming otherwise for a subject like History, where marks depend heavily on essay quality and judgment under time pressure, should be questioned. IB Gram does not publish tutor ratings or tutor counts and does not promise a specific outcome. What is offered is a considered match based on the student's actual stage and gaps, a transparent first session, and a clear way to request a different tutor if progress stalls. Genuine improvement depends on consistency and honest gap-closing, not a marketing claim.

faqs.question: My child struggles with essay writing more than remembering facts — does that change the tutoring approach?
faqs.answer: Yes, considerably. A student who recalls facts well but struggles to build an argument needs sessions focused on structuring evidence, using source material to support a point, and practising under timed conditions, rather than more content revision. This is a common pattern in History specifically, since the exam rewards argument and judgment as much as knowledge. Mentioning this distinction clearly when requesting a match helps IB Gram propose a tutor whose teaching style actually addresses writing technique, not just subject content.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with both IGCSE History and English A?
faqs.answer: Sometimes as two coordinated tutors rather than reliably as one person. Essay-structuring skills do transfer between the two subjects, and a tutor aware of both can spot the same writing habit showing up in each, but strong historical argument and strong literary analysis are different skills, and a tutor excellent at one is not automatically excellent at the other. It is worth requesting both subjects and letting IB Gram match each to the right specialist rather than assuming one tutor should cover both by default.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my child are not a good fit?
faqs.answer: This is treated as a normal outcome, not a problem to justify. If a session or two makes it clear the pace, teaching style or personality does not suit your child, you can ask IB Gram for a different tutor. Being specific about what did not work — too fast, too rigid, not enough feedback on essays — helps shape who gets suggested next, so the second match is genuinely different rather than repeating the same mismatch under a new name.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram work with students at The British School, American Embassy School or DPS International Saket?
faqs.answer: IB Gram can review tutoring requests from families at these schools and others across Delhi, but it is an independent platform and is not officially affiliated with The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School or DPS International Saket unless specifically stated. Tutors familiar with a school's general calendar and assessment rhythm can sometimes plan a revision timeline more smoothly, but this is a scheduling convenience, not a claim of partnership, and any such relationship should be verified directly with the school.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring as effective as home tutoring for History?
faqs.answer: For this subject, often yes, and sometimes more so. History tutoring relies heavily on reading documents, planning essays and reviewing marked work, all of which transfer cleanly to a shared screen. What online tutoring cannot replicate is the presence effect some younger students need to stay focused, so a family should weigh the student's own study habits rather than assuming one mode is universally better. Many Delhi families choose online specifically to avoid losing an evening slot to traffic, which matters most in the weeks right before a mock or exam.

introSummary: An IGCSE ICT tutor in Delhi needs to do something a classroom teacher rarely has time for: sit beside one student while they build a database, format a long document correctly, or debug a website authoring task, instead of moving thirty students through the same instructions at the same pace. Delhi adds its own complication — families spread across South Delhi, central Delhi and NCR towns like Gurugram or Noida need a tutor who fits real school-run timings, not an idealised slot. IB Gram matches by grade, school and how far a family can realistically stretch.

contentBlocks.heading: What a School's ICT Teacher Cannot Realistically Do for One Student
contentBlocks.body: A school ICT teacher in Delhi is usually managing a full class through the same practical exercise at the same time — everyone building the same spreadsheet, everyone formatting the same mail-merge document — because that is the only way to run a lab period for thirty students. That structure works for introducing a skill. It does not work for the student who fell behind two topics ago, or the one who understood database queries instantly and is now bored waiting for the rest of the class to catch up. A tutor's job is the opposite of the classroom's job: find exactly where one student's understanding breaks down, whether that is a specific database query type, a spreadsheet formula category, or confusion about which practical paper actually requires which software, and fix that one thing before moving on. This is especially true for IGCSE ICT because the subject is graded heavily on practical output — a document produced under exam conditions, a working spreadsheet model, a functioning webpage — not on essay-style demonstration of knowledge the way some other subjects are. A school teacher genuinely cannot give one student forty minutes of individual troubleshooting on a formatting error; a tutor can, and that difference is usually what separates a student who is comfortable walking into the practical exam from one who is still guessing at software steps under time pressure.
items: Classroom teaching moves the whole class through one exercise at once
A tutor isolates and fixes one student's specific practical gap
ICT is graded on working output, not essay demonstration of knowledge
Individual troubleshooting time is what a 30-student classroom cannot offer
Comfort with software steps under time pressure is the real exam skill

contentBlocks.heading: The Three Skill Areas an ICT Tutor Actually Works Through
contentBlocks.body: IGCSE ICT tutoring generally breaks into three distinct areas, and a good tutor treats each differently rather than running one generic revision session. Theory preparation covers concepts — types of network, input and output devices, data security, the social and ethical implications of ICT use — and is best tackled through past-paper question practice, because the exam rewards precise, syllabus-specific terminology over general knowledge, however sound that general knowledge is. Document production and data manipulation covers practical skills like mail merge, formatted long documents, spreadsheet formulas and functions, and database queries and reports — this is skill-building work, done at a keyboard, where a tutor watches the student execute each step rather than simply explaining it. Website authoring and presentation or data analysis tasks form the third area, testing whether a student can apply structure, navigation and formatting rules correctly under a fixed brief, again a practical skill that only improves with repeated, corrected attempts. Students often do well on one of these three areas and poorly on another — a strong theory student can still fumble spreadsheet formulas, and a confident spreadsheet user can still write vague, unspecific theory answers. A tutor's first job is identifying which of the three areas is actually weak, rather than assuming a student needs help across the board simply because a mock score was low.
items: Theory — networks, devices, data security, ethical and social implications
Document production — mail merge, long-document formatting under time limits
Data manipulation — spreadsheet formulas and functions, database queries and reports
Website authoring and presentation tasks — structure and navigation under a brief
Weakness is usually concentrated in one area, not spread evenly across all three

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to First Session — What Actually Happens
contentBlocks.body: A parent tells IB Gram the student's grade, school, target exam session and roughly where the family is based in Delhi or NCR. That last detail matters immediately for ICT specifically, because practical sessions sometimes need the student at their own computer with their own software setup, which shapes whether home tutoring, online tutoring or a mix makes more sense than it would for a purely discussion-based subject. Tutor background is checked next — genuine IGCSE ICT teaching experience, not a general computer-science tutor assuming the syllabus overlaps more than it does, since ICT's specific software and paper structure differ from computer science's programming focus. A short conversation usually follows to confirm the student's software access, exam board, and whether a school has already flagged specific weak areas from a recent mock. The first session is diagnostic: the tutor works through a short theory question and a short practical task live, watching where the student hesitates or makes an avoidable error, rather than lecturing through a slide deck. A parent should get a specific note afterward — which of the three skill areas needs the most attention, and a realistic weekly plan. If, four weeks in, a parent cannot point to a specific practical skill that has visibly improved, that is worth raising directly with the tutor rather than waiting for the next mock to reveal the same gap.

Tutor checked for genuine ICT background, not adjacent computer-science teaching
Software access and exam board confirmed before the first session
First session includes a live theory question and a live practical task
Four-week check for one specific, visible practical improvement

Within this belt, tutors who already teach practical subjects tend to prefer areas where they can bring or rely on consistent equipment, since a laptop issue mid-session wastes practical time that a purely verbal subject would not lose. Delhi traffic being what it is, a tutor confirmed for a Saket family in the evening cannot always also cover a Vasant Vihar family the same evening, so availability within these pockets is genuinely tutor-specific rather than guaranteed across the whole belt. Families in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad, commuting daily into Delhi for school, are generally better served by online tutoring for this subject, since a round trip purely for a tutoring session adds hours to an already long school day. Online tutoring for ICT works well precisely because the practical component is software-based — a tutor can watch a shared screen, walk through a spreadsheet formula or database query step by step, and correct mistakes in real time without needing to be in the same room. This is one subject where online delivery genuinely does not lose much compared with sitting side by side.

contentBlocks.heading: Where ICT Fits Across a Student's Grade Progression
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram's Delhi network supports students from Grade 1 to Grade 12, though a request for IGCSE ICT specifically almost always starts once a school confirms the subject as part of a student's Grade 9 or 10 options. Before that stage, general computer literacy support — typing, basic software familiarity, safe internet use — is a different, lighter kind of help, and a family asking too early for exam-style ICT tutoring is usually better served by a general digital-skills tutor instead. Once a student is actually enrolled in the IGCSE ICT syllabus, the two exam years demand steadily increasing practical fluency: a Grade 9 student is still learning individual skills in isolation, while a Grade 10 student close to Paper 2 and Paper 3 needs to execute multi-step practical tasks fluently, combining formatting, data manipulation and document assembly under realistic time pressure. Some Delhi students take ICT alongside heavier subjects like Math AA or Physics and treat it as a lower priority, which is a reasonable choice given limited study hours, but it becomes a problem only if that deprioritising continues right up to the practical exam, where fluency genuinely needs repeated hands-on practice rather than last-week cramming. A tutor's honest advice at this stage is usually to protect a minimum of consistent practical practice time even while another subject gets more attention.

Younger students need general digital literacy, not exam-style ICT coaching
Grade 9 — isolated skill building; Grade 10 — combined multi-step tasks
Practical fluency needs repeated hands-on time, not last-week cramming

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Recommended

A tutor who has taught programming-heavy computer science is not automatically equipped for ICT's document-production and data-manipulation focus, and this distinction is checked directly rather than assumed from a resume line. Software familiarity matters concretely: a tutor should be comfortable with the specific applications the practical papers use for spreadsheets, databases and document production, since guiding a student through an unfamiliar interface wastes session time on both sides. Scheduling reliability is checked too, particularly for Delhi families managing tight school-run windows, because a tutor who repeatedly reschedules disrupts a practical skill plan more than it disrupts a purely theory-based one. IB Gram does not publish tutor counts, ratings or promised grade outcomes; what a parent can reasonably ask for instead is specificity — which practical software has this tutor actually taught, what would the first session's diagnostic task look like, and how is progress tracked across the three skill areas. A tutor who gives a concrete, syllabus-specific answer to those questions has usually been properly vetted; one who answers only in general encouragement has not.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between a Home Tutor and an Online Specialist for a Practical Subject
contentBlocks.body: Delhi families often default to assuming a practical subject needs an in-person tutor, and that assumption is worth questioning directly for ICT. A home tutor has real advantages for a student who needs someone checking posture at the keyboard, catching small formatting mistakes by looking over a shoulder, or simply staying focused without a screen's usual distractions nearby. But online tutoring for ICT specifically loses very little, because the entire practical component is software-based and a shared screen shows exactly what a student is doing, formula by formula, click by click, just as clearly as sitting beside them would. Where online genuinely wins is subject depth and schedule flexibility — a strong ICT specialist willing to work a fixed evening slot without a Delhi traffic commute attached is often easier to keep consistent over a full term than a home tutor juggling multiple South Delhi families in one evening. Hybrid plans suit many Delhi households well: an occasional home session for a parent to see progress directly, combined with a steady weekly online rhythm for the actual skill-building work. What genuinely does not work is treating mode choice as fixed once decided — a family that started with home tutoring and finds scheduling increasingly difficult should feel free to shift some or all sessions online rather than persisting with a mode that has stopped being practical.

contentBlocks.heading: Where Academic Honesty Gets Tested in a Practical Subject
contentBlocks.body: ICT's practical papers create their own version of a familiar problem: it is entirely possible for a tutor to build a polished spreadsheet or database file for a student to submit as coursework or practice, and it is entirely wrong to do so. IB Gram expects tutors to build the student's own capability instead — walking through why a formula is structured a certain way, having the student type each step themselves even when it would be faster for the tutor to do it, and treating a slow, correct attempt as more valuable than a fast one the tutor effectively completed. This matters more in practical subjects than people sometimes assume, because a student who has only ever watched a tutor solve a problem develops false confidence that evaporates the moment they sit alone in an exam hall with no one to hand them the next step. Command-term awareness applies here too — an ICT exam question that says 'create' or 'insert' expects a specific, checkable action, and a student needs to have actually performed that action independently, repeatedly, before it becomes automatic under pressure. A reasonable way for a parent to check this honestly is to ask the student, unprompted, to repeat a practical task the tutor covered the previous week without any help; if they cannot, the session built dependency rather than skill, and that is worth raising with the tutor directly.

faqs.question: Isn't ICT just typing and using Word and Excel — does my child really need a tutor?
faqs.answer: There is more to it than everyday computer use. IGCSE ICT tests specific, exam-defined skills — precise mail-merge steps, particular spreadsheet formula types, structured database queries, formatted long documents — under timed conditions, and marking is strict about exact technique, not general competence. A student who is comfortable with computers casually can still lose significant marks for missing a specific formatting requirement or using an inefficient formula approach the mark scheme does not reward. A tutor's value is in drilling the exact exam-style execution repeatedly until it becomes automatic, which a general comfort with technology does not replace.

faqs.question: Can I get a home tutor if I live in Gurugram or Noida but my child studies in Delhi?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring is generally reviewed for South Delhi and central Delhi pockets like Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, so a Gurugram or Noida home address usually falls outside realistic home-tutor coverage given Delhi's cross-city traffic. Online tutoring is the practical answer here, and for ICT specifically it works especially well because all the practical work happens on screen already — a tutor watching your child's shared screen can correct a spreadsheet formula or database query exactly as effectively as sitting beside them. Most NCR commuter families end up choosing online for this reason rather than as a compromise.

faqs.question: What software does my child need for sessions?
faqs.answer: That depends on the specific applications your child's school and exam board use for the practical papers, which is confirmed during matching before the first session so the tutor and student are working in the same environment. Mismatched software between what a tutor teaches and what the exam actually uses creates real problems, since interface differences can cost time in the actual exam even when the underlying skill is understood. If you are unsure which applications your child's school uses, checking with the school directly before the first session avoids wasted early sessions built around the wrong tools.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE ICT tutoring cost in Delhi?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by tutor experience, session mode and how many sessions a week the plan needs, so there is no single Delhi-wide figure to quote without those specifics. Home tutoring in South Delhi pockets typically costs more than online sessions once a tutor's travel time is factored in, particularly during peak traffic hours. IB Gram shares an actual fee range once a tutor is matched to your child's grade, school and mode, so you can weigh it against your budget honestly before agreeing to a term-length plan rather than after the first session's invoice.

faqs.question: What if my child and the tutor don't get along?
faqs.answer: Raise it with IB Gram directly rather than pushing through a mismatch out of politeness, especially in a practical subject where a student needs to feel comfortable asking basic software questions without embarrassment. A replacement tutor can be reviewed using the same matching criteria — verified ICT background, software familiarity and realistic scheduling — with the earlier mismatch noted so the next match accounts for it. This is a normal part of finding the right fit, not a sign that tutoring itself has failed, and addressing it early costs far less time than persisting through a full term of poor engagement.

faqs.question: My child is behind with only two months to the exam. Can a tutor fix this?
faqs.answer: Two months is enough time to make a real difference, but be realistic about what kind of difference. A tutor can sharpen exam technique, close specific gaps in one or two practical skill areas, and drill theory terminology precisely — this genuinely improves marks. What two months cannot do is build deep practical fluency from near-zero hands-on practice; that needs repeated hours at the keyboard that simply cannot be compressed. The honest plan is triage: identify the highest-value gaps first, drill those intensively, and accept that some lower-priority practical skills may only get a lighter pass.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with The British School, American Embassy School or DPS International Saket?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School, DPS International Saket, or any other school. These schools are mentioned only because families connected to them commonly search for ICT tutoring support, not because of any partnership. faqs.question: How many sessions a week does ICT usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on how many of the three skill areas — theory, document and data manipulation, and website or presentation authoring — currently need work, and how close the exam is. A student with one clear weak area often manages with one focused session a week. A student weak across two or three areas, or within a few months of Paper 2 and Paper 3, usually benefits from two sessions, split between practical drilling and theory revision. More than two rarely helps unless a specific coursework or practice deadline is approaching.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work as well as home tutoring for a computer subject?
faqs.answer: For ICT specifically, yes, more reliably than most parents expect. The entire practical component happens on a screen already, so a tutor watching a shared screen sees exactly what your child is doing — every formula, every click — as clearly as sitting beside them would. What online cannot replace is a parent's ability to glance over and see progress directly, which is why some Delhi families choose an occasional home session alongside a mainly online plan. But in terms of actual skill transfer for spreadsheets, databases and document production, online tutoring holds up well.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with other subjects like Math or Physics alongside ICT?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the tutor genuinely has strong background in both, which is worth confirming directly rather than assuming any tutor covers multiple subjects equally well. IB Gram's Delhi network includes tutors across ICT alongside Math AA, Math AI, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English, so a combined match is possible where it genuinely fits. For a student close to exams in more than one subject, though, a single dedicated ICT specialist paired with a separate specialist for the other subject usually produces stronger results than one tutor spread thin across both.

Home tutoring may be possible in select South and Central Delhi pockets; online tutoring works across the whole city and NCR. contentBlocks.heading: The Commute Question Comes Before the Subject Question in Delhi
contentBlocks.body:
Most tutoring pages start with the subject. In Delhi, that order is backwards. A family in Greater Kailash searching for a Mathematics A tutor is not really asking "who is the best tutor in the city" — a genuinely strong tutor based in, say, Chanakyapuri may be functionally unavailable on a Tuesday evening if the route between the two crosses peak traffic. So the first useful thing IB Gram does is separate the question of subject fit from the question of physical reach, because conflating them is exactly how families end up with a tutor who is excellent on paper and unreliable in practice.

Delhi's IB and IGCSE tutoring demand is shaped by embassy communities, international school families, and students who cross NCR daily for school, which means schedules are already tight before tutoring is added. A student commuting from Noida or Gurugram to a Delhi school does not have much slack left for an inconvenient home-tutoring slot squeezed in after a long day. Recognising this upfront, rather than after a few missed or rescheduled sessions, is what separates a workable plan from one that quietly falls apart by the third week.

A strong tutor stuck in traffic is not actually an available tutor

contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be possible in select South Delhi, Central Delhi and nearby residential pockets, and it works best when a tutor already teaches in that general zone rather than being asked to cross the city specifically for one family. For a younger student, roughly in the Grade 6 to 8 range, in-person sessions can help with focus and give a parent direct visibility into how the tutor works, which matters more at that age than pure subject specialisation. But this only holds where the travel is genuinely reasonable — home tutoring stretched across a long, traffic-heavy route tends to produce cancelled sessions, not consistent progress.

Online tutoring is available across Delhi and NCR for all supported subjects, and for Mathematics A specifically, it removes the travel constraint entirely from the equation of finding the right specialist. A student needing focused, methodical support on a specific topic — coordinate geometry, or a particular algebra technique — can access a tutor strong in exactly that area regardless of which part of the city they teach from. Many Delhi families land on a hybrid approach: a home tutor for regular weekly grounding where travel allows it, and online sessions for short, intensive revision cycles before school mocks. The honest trade-off is that hybrid needs more coordination between two schedules, and it is not necessary for a family that finds one mode works fine on its own.

contentBlocks.heading: Mathematics A Rarely Travels Alone in a Delhi Household
contentBlocks.body:
Families approaching IB Gram about Mathematics A in Delhi are frequently also managing Physics, Chemistry, Economics or English A, whether for the same student balancing multiple subject deadlines or for a sibling on a different track entirely. Many Delhi students are also juggling extracurricular commitments alongside school deadlines, which means a family coordinating three tutors independently often ends up with scheduling collisions nobody planned for — a Wednesday evening booked twice, a Thursday left empty. Coordinating this centrally, rather than leaving each subject relationship to arrange itself, tends to produce a more sustainable week.

There is also a real academic overlap worth naming. Math AA and Math AI students at Diploma level often share foundational algebra and functions weaknesses with IGCSE Mathematics A students one or two years younger, and a tutor who teaches across both levels sometimes spots a gap earlier than a tutor working with only one age group. This is not a reason to bundle subjects by default — a family needing only Mathematics A support should get exactly that, nothing more. But where a household genuinely has more than one need, IB Gram uses this context to avoid scheduling collisions and to flag skill overlaps a tutor working in isolation might miss.

But proximity on a map is not the same as proximity in practice. Vasant Vihar to Saket is a reasonable distance in isolation, yet the actual drive time depends heavily on the hour, and a tutor who can make a 4pm slot easily may struggle with a 6pm one during peak traffic. Chanakyapuri's diplomatic-zone roads carry their own timing quirks that a tutor unfamiliar with the area may not anticipate. A younger sibling in the same household, in the Primary Years range, needs an entirely different kind of support — early numeracy and unit-of-inquiry groundwork rather than formal algebra or geometry, though a genuine comfort with mathematical thinking built early does make the transition into Mathematics A noticeably smoother a few years later.

What IB Gram does offer is a transparent process: a diagnostic first session, a tutor background genuinely checked against the specification, and a clear route to switching if a match is not working after a fair trial. faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic if we live in Chanakyapuri but the tutor is based near Saket?
faqs.answer: It depends on the intended session time more than the raw distance. Chanakyapuri to Saket is workable outside peak hours but can stretch considerably during evening traffic, which is exactly when most tutoring slots are needed. IB Gram checks a tutor's actual base against your preferred slot before suggesting them, rather than assuming neighbourhood proximity guarantees reliability. faqs.question: What does an IGCSE Mathematics A tutor's fees in Delhi typically depend on?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the tutor's experience level, whether sessions are home-based or online, and session frequency and length. A home tutor factoring in South or Central Delhi travel time may price differently from a purely online specialist. IB Gram does not set one fixed rate across all tutors; exact fees are confirmed directly with the shortlisted tutor before any sessions begin, based on the specific plan agreed.

faqs.question: My child commutes daily from Gurugram or Noida to school in Delhi. Does that limit tutoring options?
faqs.answer: It shapes the options more than it limits them. A student already spending significant time commuting to school usually has less patience for a lengthy additional trip for tutoring, which is where online sessions tend to work better than adding a home visit onto an already long day. Some families do a home session on weekends when travel time isn't competing with school hours, combined with online sessions on weekdays.

faqs.question: We've had a month of sessions with no real improvement. What now?
faqs.answer: Four weeks in, there should be something specific to point to — fewer errors on a particular topic, better exam-technique habits, or at minimum a clearly named remaining gap with a plan. If none of that is visible, raise it directly with IB Gram and consider switching tutors rather than continuing on hope. A mismatch in teaching style is common and is far easier to fix early than after a full term has passed.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work as well as home tutoring for Mathematics specifically?
faqs.answer: For most Mathematics A needs, yes — a tutor can share a digital whiteboard, work through problems step by step, and review a student's written script just as precisely as they could across a table. Where online can struggle more is with younger students who need frequent redirection to stay focused, which is one honest reason home tutoring still suits some families better, particularly at the younger end of the age range.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with The British School New Delhi or the American Embassy School?

These names describe general area context and cohort patterns only. Any specific claim a tutor makes about familiarity with a school's assessment style should be checked directly with that tutor.

faqs.question: How does IB Gram verify a Mathematics A tutor's actual subject knowledge?
faqs.answer: Through direct discussion of the specification's topic areas and the command-term language examiners use, and by confirming the tutor can explain precisely why a sample answer would lose marks under the actual mark scheme. This is checked before a tutor is suggested to any family, not assumed from a general Mathematics teaching background or degree title alone.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor handle both my child's IGCSE Mathematics A and a younger sibling's primary-level maths?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but this is confirmed case by case rather than assumed. The two need genuinely different approaches — early numeracy and inquiry-based learning for a younger child versus algebraic and problem-solving depth for a Mathematics A student. IB Gram only suggests one tutor across both children where that tutor's background actually supports both levels well, not as a scheduling convenience.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the first Mathematics A tutoring session?
faqs.answer: The tutor reviews a recent test, homework script, or a set of practice problems with the student to identify exactly where marks or understanding are being lost, rather than beginning with a generic introductory lesson. This gives the parent a concrete, written starting point and gives the tutor real information to build the following weeks' plan around, instead of guessing at the gaps.

faqs.question: Is a hybrid plan of home and online sessions worth the extra coordination in Delhi?
faqs.answer: For some families, yes — particularly where a weekly home session builds routine and a periodic online session accesses deeper subject specialism before a mock exam. For a family that already finds one mode working well, adding the other mainly adds scheduling complexity without a clear benefit. It is worth considering specifically around exam-heavy periods rather than adopting as a permanent default.

heroTitle: IGCSE Mathematics Tuition in Delhi
heroSubtitle: Before hiring anyone, a parent needs three answers: which topics are actually weak, whether a home tutor's travel time across Delhi traffic is realistic, and whether Math AA or Math AI is even the right track ahead.
introSummary: The honest first question before booking an IGCSE Mathematics tutor in Delhi isn't which tutor is best-rated - it's what exactly is going wrong. A student scoring inconsistently on algebra but solid on geometry needs a different tutor than one who understands concepts but runs out of time in every timed paper. IB Gram works with families across Grade 1 to Grade 12 in Delhi, from Vasant Vihar to Saket to families managing a commute from Gurugram or Noida, and starts every enquiry by identifying the actual gap before suggesting a name.

contentBlocks.heading: The Diagnostic Question Every Delhi Parent Should Ask First
contentBlocks.body:
Ask a parent why they're looking for an IGCSE Mathematics tutor in Delhi and the answer is almost always a symptom, not a diagnosis: 'his grades are dropping,' or 'she panics in timed tests.' Neither tells you what to actually fix. A student who understands a topic in class but blanks under time pressure needs paper-practice and pacing drills, not another round of concept explanation. A student who genuinely hasn't grasped a topic - often algebraic manipulation or coordinate geometry - needs the opposite: slower teaching before any timed practice makes sense.

Delhi adds a second layer most other cities don't: geography genuinely constrains which tutor is realistic. A family in Vasant Vihar considering a tutor based in Saket is looking at real evening traffic, not a theoretical fifteen-minute drive. A family split between school in central Delhi and home in Gurugram or Noida faces this even more sharply, since the same tutor may or may not be able to sustain a weekly commute across that distance.

So before comparing tutor profiles, a parent gets more value from answering two questions honestly: what specific topic or exam skill is the actual problem, and is home tutoring geographically realistic for this family's week, or does online make more sense regardless of preference.
items: Symptom (falling grades) is not the same as diagnosis (weak topic)
Time-pressure problems need pacing drills, not more explanation
Delhi traffic makes home-tutor geography a real constraint
Answer the gap and the geography question before comparing tutors

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Turns Those Two Answers Into a Shortlist
contentBlocks.body:
Once a family can name the actual gap - say, coordinate geometry and algebraic fractions - and the realistic mode - home tutoring limited to a specific South Delhi pocket, or online without geographic constraint - IB Gram builds a shortlist around both rather than either alone. A tutor strong in geometry but only available two evenings a week that don't fit the family's schedule isn't actually a match, however good their profile reads.

Subject depth gets checked specifically against the weak topic named, not just general IGCSE Mathematics competence. A tutor excellent at calculus-adjacent topics for older students isn't automatically the right fit for a Grade 9 student struggling with basic algebraic manipulation; the teaching style needed is genuinely different.

A first session is used to confirm the diagnosis the parent gave matches what the tutor actually observes - sometimes a 'panics under time pressure' turns out to be a content gap dressed up as anxiety, or the reverse. That first-session finding gets shared with the parent plainly, even when it revises the original assumption that started the search.

If the shortlist doesn't produce a workable match on the first attempt - schedule conflict, personality mismatch, or a tutor whose depth doesn't quite fit the actual gap - IB Gram treats that as normal course-correction, not a failed search.
items: Shortlist built around named gap plus realistic mode together
Subject depth checked against the specific weak topic
First session confirms or revises the original diagnosis
A failed first shortlist is course-correction, not failure

contentBlocks.heading: Which Parts of IGCSE Mathematics Actually Cause the Trouble
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE Mathematics covers number, algebra, geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, statistics and, depending on the tier, some calculus groundwork. In practice, a small handful of topics generate most tutoring requests: algebraic manipulation and factorisation, coordinate geometry, trigonometric ratios in non-right-angled contexts, and probability involving combined events. A tutor's general strength across the syllabus matters less than whether they can specifically unpick whichever of these is the student's actual block.

Delhi families frequently ask, in the same conversation, about tutors for the subjects a student will carry into the IB Diploma Programme afterward - Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A appear often enough that IB Gram's Delhi network places tutors for all of them, usually through separate specialists rather than one person covering everything.

Choosing between Math AA and Math AI matters earlier than most families realise; a Grade 10 student still uncertain about this track benefits from a tutor who can speak honestly about which pathway suits their actual strengths, algebraic fluency versus applied and technology-based problem solving, rather than defaulting to whichever track is more commonly chosen at their school. That conversation is worth having before Grade 11 registration deadlines force a decision under pressure.
items: Algebraic manipulation and factorisation cause frequent trouble
Coordinate geometry and non-right-angle trigonometry are common blocks
Same network covers Math AA/AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, English A for DP-track families
Math AA vs Math AI choice deserves an honest conversation before Grade 11

contentBlocks.heading: Grade Range, School Calendars and When to Start Looking
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram works with Delhi families from Grade 1 through Grade 12, spanning a Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, a Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and a Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19 in schools that offer the full pathway. IGCSE Mathematics itself usually sits within the Grade 9-10 band, often the two years where a student's confidence with the subject either consolidates or genuinely starts to slip.

May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions give Delhi families two natural planning horizons; a student sitting the November session has a materially different runway than one aiming for May, and starting tutoring six months out looks very different from starting six weeks out. Waiting until after a disappointing mock result is common, but it isn't the only sensible time to start - some of the strongest results come from families who acted on early warning signs from regular school assessments rather than the mock itself.

For younger students still in the Primary or early Middle Years stage, Mathematics tutoring in Delhi is less about exam technique and more about not letting small gaps compound quietly for two or three years before IGCSE makes them visible and urgent all at once.
items: Grade 1-12 supported; IGCSE Math typically Grade 9-10
May and November 2026 sessions are the two planning horizons
Acting on early school assessment warnings beats waiting for a bad mock
Early Primary/Middle Years gaps compound quietly if left unaddressed

contentBlocks.heading: South and Central Delhi Pockets, and When Online Wins Instead
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be reviewed in Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, along with nearby residential pockets such as Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh. These South and central Delhi areas carry a meaningful share of the city's international-school population, which is part of why IGCSE Mathematics tutoring demand concentrates here.

Even within this core, though, home tutoring isn't automatically the right call. A tutor based in Saket reaching a family in Chanakyapuri during evening traffic may lose thirty to forty minutes each way, time that could otherwise be spent teaching, and that reality should factor into the decision rather than being discovered after the first few sessions run late.

Families commuting from Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad into Delhi schools face an even sharper version of this problem, since a home tutor's travel simply isn't realistic across that distance on a weekday evening. Online tutoring removes this constraint entirely and stays available across Delhi and the wider NCR without the same geographic ceiling - which is precisely why it's often not a compromise but the more sensible first choice for families in this exact situation, not just a fallback for whoever couldn't find a nearby tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: Choosing Between a Home Tutor and an Online Specialist
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi families often end up choosing hybrid support rather than picking one mode permanently: a home tutor for weekly accountability where travel is genuinely realistic, and an online specialist when subject depth or scheduling flexibility matters more than physical presence. This isn't indecision - it's usually the correct answer once the actual constraints are laid out honestly.

Home tutoring suits a younger student who benefits from someone physically present to catch confusion early, or a family that specifically wants in-person accountability for a student who tends to drift during unsupervised study time. Online tutoring suits a family chasing a specific specialist - someone genuinely strong at the exact topic causing trouble - regardless of where in Delhi or NCR that tutor happens to live, and it holds up better for short, intensive revision cycles before a mock exam when scheduling flexibility matters more than routine.

The honest trade-off: a home tutor sees body language and can adjust pace mid-sentence in a way video sometimes misses, particularly with a student who won't say 'I'm lost' out loud. A parent weighing this should be clear about which matters more for their specific child, rather than assuming one mode is simply superior for every family in Delhi.
items: Hybrid is often the correct answer, not a compromise
Home tutoring suits younger or easily-distracted students
Online suits chasing a specific specialist and short revision cycles
Trade-off: video can miss subtle signs of a lost student

contentBlocks.heading: How to Tell in a Month Whether the Diagnosis Was Right
contentBlocks.body:
The clearest sign a match is working isn't a grade jump in four weeks - that's too soon to expect reliably - it's whether the tutor's own read of the problem, given after the first session, matches what the parent already suspected, or offers a genuinely more precise version of it. A tutor who says 'trigonometric ratios in obtuse-angle problems specifically' is giving a more useful answer than one who says 'needs to practice more.'

By the end of four weeks, a parent should see the named gap actually narrowing in a way that shows up in the student's own worked examples, not just in a tutor's verbal reassurance. If a student was struggling with algebraic fractions, they should be visibly more confident setting up the working correctly, even if they still make occasional errors - confidence in approach matters as much as accuracy at this stage.

If nothing has changed in that specific, named area by week four, that's a legitimate reason to revisit the diagnosis itself, not just swap tutors and hope for a different result with the same assumed problem. Sometimes the original diagnosis was simply wrong, and that's worth admitting rather than treating tutor changes as the only available fix. No result here is ever guaranteed in advance - IB Gram won't claim otherwise.

Week-four check: is the named gap narrowing in the student's own work

A conversation with IB Gram moves faster when a parent brings three things: the student's grade and current school, a specific description of what's going wrong rather than a general complaint, and an honest read on whether home tutoring is geographically realistic for the family's week or whether online makes more sense from the start.

None of these need to be perfectly worked out in advance - 'I think it's something about geometry but I'm not fully sure' is a completely fine starting point, since the first session is designed to sharpen exactly that. What matters is bringing whatever specific evidence exists: a recent test paper, a comment from the school, a pattern the parent has noticed over a few weeks.

From there, IB Gram builds a shortlist and explains, briefly, why each name was chosen for this particular gap and schedule, rather than handing over a generic list of available tutors. A parent stays in control of the decision at every step, and there's no obligation to commit to an ongoing plan before a first diagnostic session confirms the match actually makes sense for this specific student.

faqs.answer: This is worth deciding with input from both the school and a tutor who knows the student's actual working style, not just their current grade. Math AA suits a student comfortable with abstract algebraic manipulation and proof-style reasoning; Math AI suits one who prefers applied, technology-assisted problem solving and real-world contexts. A tutor working with the student through Grade 10 IGCSE Mathematics can usually offer a genuinely informed read on this before the Grade 11 registration deadline forces the decision.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor better than online for IGCSE Mathematics, or does it not matter?
faqs.answer: It depends more on the student than on the subject. A student who drifts without someone physically present, or who needs body-language cues to know when to slow down, benefits from home tutoring where the family's Delhi location makes travel realistic. A student who is reasonably focused and mainly needs access to a specific subject specialist regardless of location usually does just as well online, sometimes better, since online opens up tutors who aren't limited by which part of Delhi they can reach on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: My child's school is in Chanakyapuri but we live near Gurugram - what's realistic?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring across that distance on a weekday evening usually isn't realistic once school pick-up, homework and traffic are all accounted for, even if a tutor is technically willing to attempt it once or twice. Online tutoring removes that constraint and tends to work better for families in exactly this situation, since it opens access to a strong IGCSE Mathematics specialist without depending on which part of NCR they happen to live in. Some Gurugram and Noida families also choose a hybrid plan with occasional in-person sessions during a school holiday.

faqs.question: What if the tutor's diagnosis of the problem doesn't match what I expected?
faqs.answer: That's actually useful information, not a red flag. A parent's sense of the problem, formed from grades and general observation, is sometimes accurate and sometimes an educated guess; a tutor sitting with the student directly can often narrow it further after just one session. IB Gram asks tutors to share this plainly rather than simply agreeing with whatever the parent originally assumed, since teaching toward the wrong diagnosis wastes everyone's time. If the revised read still doesn't feel right after discussion, that's worth raising directly before committing to an ongoing plan.

faqs.question: Which Delhi areas can actually get a home tutor for Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring may be reviewed in Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket, Chanakyapuri and nearby pockets including Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh, depending on a specific tutor's travel range. Families further out, including much of Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad, are generally better served by online tutoring, which stays available across the wider NCR without the same distance limitation. It's worth asking directly during the enquiry rather than assuming either way based on area alone.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor also help with Physics or another subject later?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, though most tutors specialise and a strong Mathematics tutor isn't automatically the right fit for Physics or Economics as well. IB Gram's Delhi network separately covers Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A for families moving into the IB Diploma Programme, usually matched through a different specialist per subject. It's fine to mention a second subject during the same enquiry; it's simply treated as a separate matching request rather than assumed to be the same tutor's job.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session if we're not fully sure what's wrong?
faqs.answer: That's a normal starting point, not a problem. The first session is diagnostic - the tutor works through a mix of topics and a short timed exercise to see where the student's actual confidence breaks down, which is sometimes different from what grades alone suggest. The parent gets a plain summary afterward: which topic or skill is the real issue, and what the next few weeks should focus on. This shapes the ongoing plan instead of guessing from a report card alone.

faqs.question: Can we change the plan if my child's needs shift closer to the exam session?
faqs.answer: Yes - a plan built six months before the May or November exam session should look different from one built six weeks out, and IB Gram expects this to shift rather than treating the original plan as fixed. As mock results come in or coursework deadlines shift, it's worth flagging changes to the tutor directly so the weekly focus can adjust, whether that means more timed past-paper practice or returning to a topic that resurfaces under exam conditions. A rigid plan that ignores this kind of signal usually serves the tutor's convenience more than the student's actual needs.
